[[annex-D]]
[appendix]
== Feature Catalogue

=== Sea Ice

Sea Ice is an area at sea that is covered, in whole or in part, with ice.

* *Total Concentration* (ICEACT): ICEACT specifies the total concentration of ice in an area. It represents the ratio expressed in tenths describing the total area of the water surface covered by ice as a fraction of the whole area.
* *Partial Concentration* (ICEAPC): ICEAPC specifies the partial concentrations of ice in an area. (‘Ca, Cband Cc’).
* *Ice Stage of Development* (ICESOD): Ice Stage of Development describes the ages and thicknesses of the ice (‘So, Sa, Sb, Sc and Sd’).
* *Floe Sizes* (ICEFLZ): Floe Sizes describe the predominate forms of ice floe sizes (Fa, Fb and Fc) corresponding to the ice Stages of Development Sa, Sb and Screspectively.
* *Concentration of Strips and Patches* (ICESPC): A strip is a long narrow area of floating ice, about 1 kilometre or less in width, usually composed of small fragments detached from the main mass of ice, and run together under the influence of wind, swell or current. If the area of ice becomes more rounded in shape, it is referred to as a patch. ICESPC indicates the concentration in tenths within the area of Strips and Patches.
* *Level Ice* (ICELVL): ICELVL is an indication as to whether or not the ice has been affected by deformation
* *Compacting Strength* (ICECST): ICECST is an indication of strength of the compacting of the ice.
* *Ice Fracture Type* (ICEFTY): ICEFTY indicates the type of fracture, based upon width.
* *Ice Drift Speed* (ICEDSP): ICEDSP describes the speed in knots at which an ice mass is traveling.
* *Ice Drift Direction* (ICEDDR): ICEDDR indicates the direction in which an ice mass is drifting.
* *Ice Ridge Concentration* (ICERCN): ICERCN describes the concentration of hummocked ice in an ice area. Up to three values may be given in the list to correspond to the partial concentrations in ICEAPC.
* *Ice Ridge Frequency* (ICERFQ): ICERFQ indicates the frequency of ice ridges in number per nautical mile
* *Ice Ridge Mean Height* (ICERMH): ICERMH indicates the mean height of ice ridge(s) in decimetres.
* *Ice Ridge Maximum Height* (ICERXH): ICERMT indicates the maximum height of ice ridge(s) in decimetres.
* *Ice Ridge Classification* (ICERDV): ICERDV describes the predominant type of ice ridge(s) present.
* *Ice Keel Concentration* (ICEKCN): ICEKCN describes the concentration of ice keels beneath an ice area.
* *Ice Average Thickness* (ICETCK): Ice Average Thickness defines the average thickness of the ice.
* *Maximum Ice Thickness* (ICEMAX): ICEMAX specifies the maximum thickness of the ice.
* *Mimimum Ice Tickness* (ICEMIN): ICEMIN specifies the minimum thickness of the ice.
* *Ice Thickness Type* (ICETTY): ICETTY indicated whether the thickness of the ice was measured or estimated.
* *Melt Stage* (ICEMLT): The Stage of Melt describes the stages of the melting ice. Puddle: An accumulation of water on ice, mainly due to the melting of snow, but in some more advanced stages also the melting of ice. Thaw Hole: Vertical holes formed in ice when surface puddles melt through to the underlying water. Dried Ice: Ice surface from which water has disappeared after the formation of cracks and thaw holes. During the process of drying the surface whitens. Rotten Ice: Ice which has become honey-combed and is in an advanced state of disintegration. Flooded Ice: Ice which has been flooded and is heavily loaded by water or water and wet snow. Frozen Puddle: A puddle which has frozen over.
* *Snow Cover Concentration* (ICESCN): ICESCN indicates the concentration (aerial coverage) of snow in tenths.
* *Snow Depth* (ICESCT): ICESCT specifies the depth of snow cover on the ice.
* *Direction of Sastrugi* (ICEDOS): ICEDOS indicates the bearing of a sastrugi. Sastrugi are sharp, irregular ridges formed on a snow surface by wind erosion and deposition. On mobile floating ice the ridges are parallel to the direction of the wind at the time they were formed.
* *Ice Lead Status* (ICELST): The Ice Lead Status indicates the surface nature of the lead.
* *Frequency of Leads or Fractures* (ICELFQ): ICERFQ indicates the frequency of leads or fractures in number per nautical mile.
* *Orientation of Leads or Fractures* (ICELOR): ICELOR indicates the predominant orientation of leads and fractures.
* *Ice Lead (or Fracture or Crack) Width* (ICELWD): ICELWD indicates the width of a lead or fracture or crack in metres.
* *Combination Ice Stage of Development and Floe Size for the 1st partial concentration* (IA_SFA): IA_SFA describes combination(s) of Ice Stage of Development and Floe Size for the first partial concentration in an ice area. Up to three (stage of development / form of ice) combinations are allowed to describe the ice in the first partial concentration group.
* *Combination Ice Stage of Development and Floe Size for the 2nd partial concentration* (IA_SFB): IA_SFB describes combination(s) of Ice Stage of Development and Floe Size for the first partial concentration in an ice area. Up to three (stage of development / form of ice) combinations are allowed to describe the ice in the first partial concentration group.
* *Combination Ice Stage of Development and Floe Size for the 3rd partial concentration* (IA_SFC): IA_SFC describes combination(s) of Ice Stage of Development and Floe Size for the first partial concentration in an ice area. Up to three (stage of development / form of ice) combinations are allowed to describe the ice in the first partial concentration group.
* *Ice Breccia for the first partial concentration* (IA_FFA): Ice breccia is pieces of ice of different ages frozen together. IA _FFA describes the combination(s) of Ice Stage of Development and Floe Size for the first partial concentration in an ice area. Up to three (stage of development / form of ice) combinations plus the age of the younger ice consolidating the main pieces are allowed to describe the ice in the first partial concentration group.
* *Ice Breccia for the second partial concentration* (IA_FFB): Ice breccia is pieces of ice of different ages frozen together. IA _FFA describes the combination(s) of Ice Stage of Development and Floe Size for the first partial concentration in an ice area. Up to three (stage of development / form of ice) combinations plus the age of the younger ice consolidating the main pieces are allowed to describe the ice in the first partial concentration group.
* *Ice Breccia for the third partial concentration* (IA_FFC): Ice breccia is pieces of ice of different ages frozen together. IA _FFA describes the combination(s) of Ice Stage of Development and Floe Size for the first partial concentration in an ice area. Up to three (stage of development / form of ice) combinations plus the age of the younger ice consolidating the main pieces are allowed to describe the ice in the first partial concentration group.
* *Snow cover* (IA_SNG): Snow cover describes the degree of snow cover in an ice area.
* *Stage of Melting* (IA_MLT): IA_MLT describes the stage of melting according to the 5-point Russian national scale
* *Contamination* (IA_PLG): IA_PLG describes the degree of contamination (aerial coverage) in thirds based on the Russian national 3-point scale.
* *Hills Concentration* (IA_HLG): IA_HLG describes the degree of hilling in an ice area (usually multi-year ice).
* *Fractures Concentration* (IA_DUG): IA_DUG describes the degree of disunity in an ice area.

* *Lake Ice Stage of Development* (ICELSO): Lake Ice Stages of Development describe the ages and thicknesses of lake ice. (‘So, Sa, Sb, Sc and Sd’)
* *Floe Sizes* (ICEFLZ): Floe Sizes describe the predominate forms of ice floe sizes (Fa, Fb and Fc) corresponding to the ice Stages of Development Sa, Sb and Screspectively.

* *Ice Ridge Classification* (ICERDV): ICERDV describes the predominant type of ice ridge(s) present.

* *Maximum Ice Thickness* (ICEMAX): ICEMAX specifies the maximum thickness of the ice.
* *Mimimum Ice Tickness* (ICEMIN): ICEMIN specifies the minimum thickness of the ice.

=== Iceberg Area

An Iceberg Area is an area at sea in which icebergs, bergy bits, or growlers are present.

* *Number of Icebergs in Area* (ICEBNM): ICEBNM indicates the number of Icebergs within a specified area.
* *Iceberg Size* (ICEBSZ): The "Iceberg Size" categorizes the size of an iceberg.
* *Iceberg Concentration* (IA_BCN): IA_BCN specifies the total concentration of icebergs in an area.
* *Prevailing Iceberg Form* (IA_BFM): IA_BFM specifies the prevailing form of icebergs in an area.
* *Maximum Height of Above Water Part (iceberg/grounded hummock)* (IA_BUH): IA_BUF specifies the maximum height of an iceberg above the waterline in meters.

=== Ice Edge

The demarcation at any given time between the open sea and sea ice of any kind and in any concentration, whether fast or drifting.


=== Iceberg Limit

Limit of all known Icebergs.


=== Limit of Open Water

The demarcation at any given time between sea ice and freely navigable water, in which sea ice is present in concentrations less than 1/10.


=== Limit of All Known Ice

The limit of all known ice, including both sea ice of any kind and icebergs.


=== Line of Ice Ridge

Line of Ice Ridge is a line or wall of broken ice forced up by pressure processes.

* *Ice Ridge Classification* (ICERDV): ICERDV describes the predominant type of ice ridge(s) present.
* *Ice Ridge Mean Height* (ICERMH): ICERMH indicates the mean height of ice ridge(s) in decimetres.
* *Ice Ridge Maximum Height* (ICERXH): ICERMT indicates the maximum height of ice ridge(s) in decimetres.

=== Line of Ice Lead

Line of Ice Lead identifies any passage-way(s) through ice which is (are) navigable by surface vessels.

* *Ice Stage of Development* (ICESOD): Ice Stage of Development describes the ages and thicknesses of the ice (‘So, Sa, Sb, Sc and Sd’).
* *Number of Ice Objects* (IA_OBN): IA_OBN defines the number of ice objects (cracks, leads, fractures, icebergs).
* *Average Width of Ice Lead (or Fracture or Crack)* (ICEDVW): ICEDVW defines the average width of the lead or fracture or crack
* *Minimum Width of Ice Lead (or Fracture or Crack)* (IA_DMW): IA_DMW defines the minimum width of the lead or fracture or crack.
* *Maximum Width of Ice Lead (or Fracture or Crack)* (IA_DXW): IA_DXW defines the maximum width of the lead or fracture or crack.

=== Line of Ice Fracture

Any break or rupture through the ice cover, or through the single floe, resulting from deformation processes. Length may vary from a few meters to a few kilometers.

* *Ice Stage of Development* (ICESOD): Ice Stage of Development describes the ages and thicknesses of the ice (‘So, Sa, Sb, Sc and Sd’).
* *Number of Ice Objects* (IA_OBN): IA_OBN defines the number of ice objects (cracks, leads, fractures, icebergs).
* *Average Width of Ice Lead (or Fracture or Crack)* (ICEDVW): ICEDVW defines the average width of the lead or fracture or crack
* *Minimum Width of Ice Lead (or Fracture or Crack)* (IA_DMW): IA_DMW defines the minimum width of the lead or fracture or crack.
* *Maximum Width of Ice Lead (or Fracture or Crack)* (IA_DXW): IA_DXW defines the maximum width of the lead or fracture or crack.

=== Line of Ice Crac

Line of Ice Crack identifies any ice breakup, but no passage-way(s) for surface vessels.

* *Ice Stage of Development* (ICESOD): Ice Stage of Development describes the ages and thicknesses of the ice (‘So, Sa, Sb, Sc and Sd’).
* *Number of Ice Objects* (IA_OBN): IA_OBN defines the number of ice objects (cracks, leads, fractures, icebergs).
* *Average Width of Ice Lead (or Fracture or Crack)* (ICEDVW): ICEDVW defines the average width of the lead or fracture or crack
* *Minimum Width of Ice Lead (or Fracture or Crack)* (IA_DMW): IA_DMW defines the minimum width of the lead or fracture or crack.
* *Maximum Width of Ice Lead (or Fracture or Crack)* (IA_DXW): IA_DXW defines the maximum width of the lead or fracture or crack.

=== Ice Compacting

Pieces of ice are said to be compacting when they are subjected to a converging motion, which increases ice concentration and/or produces stresses which may result in ice deformation.

* *Compacting Strength* (ICECST): ICECST is an indication of strength of the compacting of the ice.

=== Ice Lead

Ice Lead identifies any fracture(s) or passage-way(s) through ice which is (are) navigable by surface vessels.

* *Ice Location Information* (ICELOC): ICELOC indicates whether the break is at a specific location, or whether there is a presence in the area.
* *Ice Lead Status* (ICELST): The Ice Lead Status indicates the surface nature of the lead.
* *Ice Lead (or Fracture or Crack) Width* (ICELWD): ICELWD indicates the width of a lead or fracture or crack in metres.

=== Iceberg

An Iceberg is a massive piece of ice, greatly varying in shape and showing more than 5 meters above the sea surface which has broken away from a glacier, and which may be afloat or grounded. This Object Class also includes smaller forms of glacial ice, known as “Bergy Bits” and “Growlers”, which are defined by their size Attribute. ICEBRG can indicate the location of a single iceberg or, if the attribute IA_OBN is specified and is greater than 1, multiple icebergs in the vicinity of a point.

* *Iceberg Size* (ICEBSZ): The "Iceberg Size" categorizes the size of an iceberg.
* *Ice Drift Speed* (ICEDSP): ICEDSP describes the speed in knots at which an ice mass is traveling.
* *Ice Drift Direction* (ICEDDR): ICEDDR indicates the direction in which an ice mass is drifting.
* *Number of Ice Objects* (IA_OBN): IA_OBN defines the number of ice objects (cracks, leads, fractures, icebergs).
* *Prevailing Iceberg Form* (IA_BFM): IA_BFM specifies the prevailing form of icebergs in an area.
* *Maximum Height of Above Water Part (iceberg/grounded hummock)* (IA_BUH): IA_BUF specifies the maximum height of an iceberg above the waterline in meters.

=== Floeberg

A Floeberg is a massive piece of sea ice composed of a hummock or a group of hummocks, frozen together and separated from any ice surroundings. They typically protrude up to 5 meters above the sea surface.

* *Ice Drift Speed* (ICEDSP): ICEDSP describes the speed in knots at which an ice mass is traveling.
* *Ice Drift Direction* (ICEDDR): ICEDDR indicates the direction in which an ice mass is drifting.

=== Ice Thickness

Ice Thickness provides a measure or estimate of ice thickness.

* *Ice Average Thickness* (ICETCK): Ice Average Thickness defines the average thickness of the ice.
* *Maximum Ice Thickness* (ICEMAX): ICEMAX specifies the maximum thickness of the ice.
* *Mimimum Ice Tickness* (ICEMIN): ICEMIN specifies the minimum thickness of the ice.
* *Ice Thickness Type* (ICETTY): ICETTY indicated whether the thickness of the ice was measured or estimated.

=== Ice Shear

An area of drift ice is subject to shear when the ice motion varies significantly in the direction normal to the motion, subjecting the ice to rotational forces.


=== Ice Divergence

Ice fields or floes in an area are subject to diverging or dispersive motion, thus reducing ice concentration and/or relieving stresses in the ice.


=== Ice Ridge/Hummock

An Ice Ridge is a line or wall of broken ice forced up by pressure. A Hummock is a hillock of broken ice which has been forced upward by pressure.

* *Ice Ridge Concentration* (ICERCN): ICERCN describes the concentration of hummocked ice in an ice area. Up to three values may be given in the list to correspond to the partial concentrations in ICEAPC.
* *Ice Ridge Frequency* (ICERFQ): ICERFQ indicates the frequency of ice ridges in number per nautical mile
* *Ice Ridge Mean Height* (ICERMH): ICERMH indicates the mean height of ice ridge(s) in decimetres.
* *Ice Ridge Maximum Height* (ICERXH): ICERMT indicates the maximum height of ice ridge(s) in decimetres.
* *Ice Ridge Classification* (ICERDV): ICERDV describes the predominant type of ice ridge(s) present.

=== Ice Keel/Bummock

From a submariner’s point of view, a Keel is a downward projecting ridge on the underside of the ice canopy - the counterpart of a Ridge. A Bummock is the counterpart of a hummock on the underside of the ice canopy.

* *Ice Keel Concentration* (ICEKCN): ICEKCN describes the concentration of ice keels beneath an ice area.
* *Ice Keel Frequency* (ICEKFQ): ICERFQ indicates the frequency of ice keels in number per nautical mile
* *Ice Keel Mean Depth* (ICEKMD): Indicates the mean depth of ice keels in decimetres.
* *Ice Keel Maximum Depth* (ICEKXD): ICERMT indicates the maximum depth of ice keels in decimetres.

=== Ice Drift

Motion of an ice field or floe as a result of forces such as wind and currents.

* *Ice Drift Speed* (ICEDSP): ICEDSP describes the speed in knots at which an ice mass is traveling.
* *Ice Drift Direction* (ICEDDR): ICEDDR indicates the direction in which an ice mass is drifting.

=== Ice Fracture

Any break or rupture through the ice pack, or a single floe, resulting from deformation processes. Length may vary from a few metres to many kilometres.

* *Ice Fracture Type* (ICEFTY): ICEFTY indicates the type of fracture, based upon width.
* *Ice Location Information* (ICELOC): ICELOC indicates whether the break is at a specific location, or whether there is a presence in the area.
* *Number of Ice Objects* (IA_OBN): IA_OBN defines the number of ice objects (cracks, leads, fractures, icebergs).
* *Ice Stage of Development* (ICESOD): Ice Stage of Development describes the ages and thicknesses of the ice (‘So, Sa, Sb, Sc and Sd’).
* *Average Width of Ice Lead (or Fracture or Crack)* (ICEDVW): ICEDVW defines the average width of the lead or fracture or crack
* *Minimum Width of Ice Lead (or Fracture or Crack)* (IA_DMW): IA_DMW defines the minimum width of the lead or fracture or crack.
* *Maximum Width of Ice Lead (or Fracture or Crack)* (IA_DXW): IA_DXW defines the maximum width of the lead or fracture or crack.

=== Ice Rafting

Pressure processes whereby one piece of ice overrides another.

* *Ice Rafting Concentration* (ICEFCN): ICEFCN describes the concentration of ice rafting in an ice area.

=== Jammed Brash Barrier

A strip or narrow belt of new, young or brash ice (usually 100-500 metres wide) formed at the edge of either drift or fast ice.


=== Stage of Melt

A description of the stage of melt of the ice; i.e. whether it has formed puddles on the surface and whether these have frozen.

* *Melt Stage* (ICEMLT): The Stage of Melt describes the stages of the melting ice. Puddle: An accumulation of water on ice, mainly due to the melting of snow, but in some more advanced stages also the melting of ice. Thaw Hole: Vertical holes formed in ice when surface puddles melt through to the underlying water. Dried Ice: Ice surface from which water has disappeared after the formation of cracks and thaw holes. During the process of drying the surface whitens. Rotten Ice: Ice which has become honey-combed and is in an advanced state of disintegration. Flooded Ice: Ice which has been flooded and is heavily loaded by water or water and wet snow. Frozen Puddle: A puddle which has frozen over.

=== Snow Cover

A description of the amount of snow covering the ice.

* *Snow Cover Concentration* (ICESCN): ICESCN indicates the concentration (aerial coverage) of snow in tenths.
* *Snow Depth* (ICESCT): ICESCT specifies the depth of snow cover on the ice.
* *Direction of Sastrugi* (ICEDOS): ICEDOS indicates the bearing of a sastrugi. Sastrugi are sharp, irregular ridges formed on a snow surface by wind erosion and deposition. On mobile floating ice the ridges are parallel to the direction of the wind at the time they were formed.

=== Strips and Patches

A strip is a long narrow area of floating ice, about 1 kilometre or less in width, usually composed of small fragments detached from the main mass of ice, and run together under the influence of wind, swell or current. If the area of ice becomes more rounded in shape, it is referred to as a patch.

* *Concentration of Strips and Patches* (ICESPC): A strip is a long narrow area of floating ice, about 1 kilometre or less in width, usually composed of small fragments detached from the main mass of ice, and run together under the influence of wind, swell or current. If the area of ice becomes more rounded in shape, it is referred to as a patch. ICESPC indicates the concentration in tenths within the area of Strips and Patches.

=== Grounded Hummock

Grounded Hummock identifies a hummock formation which is stranded.

* *Maximum Height of Above Water Part (iceberg/grounded hummock)* (IA_BUH): IA_BUF specifies the maximum height of an iceberg above the waterline in meters.
